stories.title: Ocean West Capital Partners Secures Extended Lease with District of Columbia
stories.excerpt: Ocean West Capital Partners executed an eight-year lease extension with the District of Columbia, through its Department of General Services, at Sentinel Square II, located at 1050 First Street NE in Washington, D.C.’s NoMa submarket. The District has been a valued tenant at Sentinel Square II for nearly a decade. Although their lease was not scheduled to expire until 2029, Ocean West proactively negotiated a long-term extension that secures the tenancy for an additional eight years while increasing the property’s weighted average lease term by nearly five years. Ocean West led the lease negotiations on behalf of ownership, coordinating closely with the District, tenant and landlord representatives. “We greatly value our long-standing relationship with the District of Columbia and are pleased to have reached an outcome that supports both the District’s continued occupancy at Sentinel Square II and ownership’s long-term objectives,” said Russ Allegrette, Chief Executive Officer and Co-Founder of Ocean West Capital Partners. The post Ocean West Capital Partners Secures Extended Lease with District of Columbia appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: D.C. Department of General Services extends lease at Sentinel Square II NoMa by 8 years through 2037
Ocean West negotiated extension early; original lease not expiring until 2029
Extension increases weighted average lease term by ~5 years, stabilizing office anchor tenant
stories.summary: Ocean West Capital Partners secured an eight-year lease extension with D.C.'s Department of General Services at Sentinel Square II (1050 First Street NE, NoMa), extending tenancy through 2037 despite the original lease not expiring until 2029. The proactive renegotiation increased the property's weighted average lease term by nearly five years. This is an office transaction with limited direct multifamily relevance.
stories.impact: Minimal relevance to multifamily development. This signals anchor tenant stability in NoMa and demonstrates steady government demand, which can support adjacent residential density in D.C.'s NoMa submarket, but the transaction itself is office-focused.

stories.title: Sentinel Real Estate Acquires Oregon Apartment Community
stories.excerpt: Sentinel Real Estate has acquired Willow Apartments, an upscale mid-rise multifamily community located in Lake Oswego, Oregon, approximately 9.5 miles southeast of Downtown Portland. Completed in 2024, the property is a 158-unit, five-story building that offers a mix of one-, two-, and three-bedroom residences. “Willow Apartments aligns with our strategy of acquiring high-quality rental communities situated in markets characterized by limited supply, strong population growth and positive economic fundamentals,” said George Tietjen, Managing Director of Sentinel. Willow Apartments is located along the Kruse Way suburban office corridor, one of Portland’s employment nodes, with convenient access to Interstate 5 and Highway 217, offering seamless connectivity to the Greater Portland metropolitan area, including downtown Portland, Beaverton and Hillsboro. The property also benefits from immediate access to nearby retail, dining and recreational amenities. If you’re reading about the multifamily industry, you should be in the room with its leaders. Connect Apartments brings together the executives featured in Connect CRE’s coverage for an afternoon of high-level insights and unmatched networking on September 22 at The Biltmore in LA. The post Sentinel Real Estate Acquires Oregon Apartment Community appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Sentinel Real Estate acquired Willow Apartments, 158-unit new 2024 mid-rise in Lake Oswego, Portland suburb
Property located 9.5 miles southeast of downtown, near Kruse Way employment corridor and I-5/217 connectivity
Strategy targets limited-supply markets with strong population growth and positive economic fundamentals
stories.summary: Sentinel Real Estate acquired Willow Apartments, a newly completed 158-unit, five-story multifamily community in Lake Oswego, Oregon, approximately 9.5 miles southeast of Portland. The property features a mix of one-, two-, and three-bedroom units and sits along the Kruse Way suburban office corridor with convenient freeway access. Sentinel cited limited supply, strong population growth, and positive economic fundamentals as acquisition drivers.
stories.impact: Demonstrates institutional capital deploying into Portland metro's suburban employment nodes ahead of continued in-migration; Lake Oswego's supply constraints and proximity to Beaverton/Hillsboro tech corridors (Intel, Oracle, others) signal sustained demand tailwinds. Buyers are locking in newly stabilized assets in limited-supply submarkets, signaling confidence in Portland's job-driven rental growth trajectory.

stories.title: Suffolk Construction Inks 19K-Lease in West Palm Beach
stories.excerpt: Suffolk Construction is moving its office within Downtown West Palm Beach after signing a 19,000-square-foot lease at the Echo boutique building. The builder will relocate to the top floor of the four-story building at 205 Datura Street, which sits adjacent to South Narcissus Avenue, the tenant announced. The new office sits about three blocks east of Suffolk’s current digs at 426 Clematis Street. “The new space reflects the caliber of experience we want to provide our employees, clients and partners while reinforcing our long-term commitment to a community,” Tom Thrasher, South Florida’s general manager at Suffolk, said in a statement. Toronto-based family office Coco Group purchased Echo for $45.7 million last year. The building includes about 71,000 square feet of office space, 10,000 square feet of ground-floor retail and a 257-space parking garage. Morning Calm Management repositioned the structure, which was built in 1925, into a mixed-use asset in 2021 before selling to the Coco Group. Representatives for the landlord did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Suffolk Construction leases 19,000 SF on top floor of Echo boutique building, West Palm Beach downtown
Coco Group (Toronto family office) purchased Echo for $45.7M in 2023; building includes 71K SF office, 10K SF retail, 257-space garage
Suffolk relocates 3 blocks east within downtown core, reinforcing long-term WPB commitment
stories.summary: Suffolk Construction signed a 19,000-square-foot lease on the top floor of Echo, a mixed-use boutique building at 205 Datura Street in downtown West Palm Beach. The Toronto-based Coco Group purchased the four-story asset for $45.7 million in 2023; it contains approximately 71,000 square feet of office, 10,000 square feet of ground-floor retail, and a 257-space parking garage. Suffolk's move represents a short relocation within downtown, signaling confidence in the office market.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily relevance. However, major regional contractor's continued downtown commitment and investment in high-caliber office space reflects confidence in South Florida's construction pipeline and economic health, which indirectly supports multifamily development feasibility in West Palm Beach and surrounding markets.

stories.title: Ventas Buys Senior Living Community in SoCal for $57M
stories.excerpt: Ventas has acquired a 136-unit senior living community in Ventura County, Calif., for $56.54 million, according to records with PropertyShark. The transaction closed July 15 for more than $415,700 per unit. JLL Capital Markets represented the seller, Chicago-based Harrison Street Asset Management, and announced the deal Tuesday, but did not disclose the name of the buyer or the value of the transaction. The property, Clearwater at Riverpark, was built in 2018 at 750 Clyde River Place in Oxnard. It includes 153,297 square feet on 3.8 acres in Oxnard’s Riverpark master-planned community, adjacent to The Collection at Riverpark, a regional shopping and entertainment complex. The residences average 809 square feet, and amenities include multiple dining venues, a swimming pool, a fitness center, a theater, and a salon and spa. Clearwater Living operates the community. The sale reflects continued institutional demand for newer senior housing properties in markets with limited development opportunities, according to JLL. Aaron Rosenzweig and Dan Baker led the brokerage team representing the seller. “Clearwater at Riverpark exemplifies the institutional-quality independent living assets that continue to attract premier capital in today’s market,” Rosenzweig said in a statement. Ventas is a real estate investment trust focused on senior housing, and is on the S&P 500. Harrison Street manages approximately $109 billion in real estate, infrastructure and credit strategies. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Ventas acquired Clearwater at Riverpark, 136-unit senior living in Oxnard, CA for $56.54M ($415.7K/unit)
Asset built 2018, 3.8 acres in Riverpark master-planned community adjacent to regional shopping complex
Institutional capital targeting newer senior housing in markets with favorable demographics
stories.summary: Ventas acquired Clearwater at Riverpark, a 136-unit senior living community in Oxnard, Ventura County, California, for $56.54 million (approximately $415,700 per unit) on July 15. The 2018-built property sits on 3.8 acres within the Riverpark master-planned community adjacent to The Collection shopping and entertainment complex. Clearwater Living operates the community, which features 153,297 square feet of space with amenities including dining, pool, fitness, theater, salon, and spa.
stories.impact: Senior housing is a distinct product type but signals institutional confidence in Ventura County's demographic tailwinds and master-planned community ecosystems. The $415.7K/unit price reflects strong institutional capital appetite for newer, amenity-rich communities in supply-constrained West Coast markets, which validates the development model for mixed-income multifamily in similar SoCal submarkets.

stories.title: Associated Bank Loans $28M for Chicago Transit-Oriented Apartment Development
stories.excerpt: Associated Bank announced the completion of a $28.35 million loan to a joint venture of North Park Ventures and SNS Realty Group for development of a new transit-oriented residential development in Chicago. The loan included funds for acquisition of the former Tortenson Glass Co. which consists of nearly 30,000 square feet of urban infill land. The five-story, 99-unit apartment building will offer 84 market-rate units and 15-affordable units. The new development will be on the east side of Sheffield between Belmont and School Streets. Demolition of the existing structures will begin shortly with completion of the new building planned for 2027. The unit mix will consist of four studios, 46 one-bedroom units, and 49 two-bedroom units.Daniel Barrins, a senior vice president with Associated Bank’s Commercial Real Estate division in Chicago, managed the loan arrangements and closing. This is the first loan Associated Bank has provided to North Park Ventures and SNS Realty Group. Stay ahead of the multifamily market at Connect Apartments. bullets: Associated Bank provides $28.35M construction loan for 99-unit transit-oriented development in Chicago, North Park area

stories.summary: Associated Bank completed a $28.35 million construction loan to a joint venture of North Park Ventures and SNS Realty Group for a transit-oriented residential development in Chicago's North Park neighborhood. The five-story, 99-unit building (84 market-rate, 15 affordable) will be built on the site of the former Tortenson Glass Co. (approximately 30,000 square feet of urban infill land) between Sheffield Avenue, Belmont, and School Streets. Demolition will begin shortly with building completion planned for 2027.
stories.impact: Signals regional lender confidence in Chicago's urban infill development fundamentals and mixed-income feasibility. Transit-oriented, infill development with affordable components reflects sustained demand in North Park and validates that Chicago lenders remain willing to finance at reasonable LTC ratios for well-located multifamily, despite broader credit tightening—important marker for pipeline visibility in the Midwest.

stories.title: Wideman Adds 35-Story Office Tower to Houston Portfolio
stories.excerpt: Wideman Co. acquired the 35-story TotalEnergies Tower at 1201 Louisiana St. from Brookfield Properties. The 850,000-square-foot tower was originally built in 1971. It has undergone numerous upgrades that included adding a fitness facility and adjacent bike room. The lobbies were previously renovated in 1996. And then Brookfield Properties kicked off renovations at what was then called Total Plaza, in 2019 and completed them in 2020. Ziegler Cooper Architects handled the redesign, which upgraded the street-level and second-floor lobbies as well as the tunnel level. Houston-based Tellepsen led the construction. The Houston Business Journal reports that Wideman Co. plans to keep the TotalEnergies Tower as a long-term hold within its portfolio. With the addition of TotalEnergies Tower, the Wideman Co., which also owns Jones on Main, now owns approximately 1.7 million square feet of office space in downtown Houston. The acquisition of TotalEnergies Tower comes just days after Williams Companies acquried its namesake 64-story, 1.4 million-square-foot Williams Tower at 2800 Post Oak Blvd. The post Wideman Adds 35-Story Office Tower to Houston Portfolio appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Wideman Co. acquired 35-story TotalEnergies Tower (850K SF, built 1971) from Brookfield Properties in Houston
Wideman now owns ~1.7M SF office in downtown Houston; acquisition part of broader portfolio consolidation
Long-term hold strategy; building underwent major renovations 2019–2020
stories.summary: Wideman Co. acquired the 35-story TotalEnergies Tower (850,000 square feet, originally built 1971) at 1201 Louisiana Street from Brookfield Properties in Houston. The property underwent significant renovations between 2019 and 2020, including lobby and street-level upgrades. With this acquisition, Wideman's downtown Houston office portfolio now totals approximately 1.7 million square feet and will be held long-term.
stories.impact: Minimal direct relevance to multifamily development. However, Wideman's continued office consolidation in downtown Houston and strategic long-term positioning suggests stabilization of that market's central business district, which can support mixed-use redevelopment and residential density catalysts in adjacent urban core submarkets over time.

stories.title: Paul Chung Departs Quinlan Development for SJP Properties
stories.excerpt: Quinlan Development Group’s Paul Chung has left the firm for a new post leading acquisition strategy for a major management and development firm. Chung has joined New York and New Jersey-based SJP Properties as head of acquisitions, a title he also held at Quinlan for over a year. At SJP, Chung will build out the company’s Class A office, industrial and residential portfolio between the two states, according to the firm. Chung started the new position in early July, according to SJP. “Paul’s experience leading acquisitions and capital market initiatives makes him an excellent addition to our team and our vision for commercial real estate across the region,” Steve Pozycki, founder and CEO of SJP, said in a statement. “His expertise will strengthen our efforts as we continue to pursue new development and opportunities.” At Quinlan, Chung was responsible for managing $1.2 billion in total capitalization and closing up to $500 million in equity and debt transactions, as well as handling due diligence for acquisitions. Now he will join SJP, which has developed and acquired more than 30 million square feet of real estate and completed $6.5 billion in transactions since it was founded in 1981. “Few developers combine the vision and execution that make SJP Properties one of the pre-eminent leaders in the industry, and its best-in-class developments reflect that,” Chung said in a statement. Prior to his tenure at Quinlan, Chung served as partner and director of acquisitions and capital markets for Solomon Builders. He also worked at Wildflower and Resource Real Estate, where he started in 2014, according to his LinkedIn profile. Quinlan did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Paul Chung departs Quinlan Development Group to lead acquisitions at SJP Properties (NY/NJ-based)
At Quinlan, managed $1.2B capitalization and closed ~$500M equity/debt transactions annually
SJP expanding Class A office, industrial, residential portfolio across New York and New Jersey
stories.summary: Paul Chung, head of acquisitions at Quinlan Development Group, has joined SJP Properties (New York and New Jersey–based firm) in the same acquisitions leadership role starting in early July. At Quinlan, Chung managed $1.2 billion in total capitalization and closed up to $500 million in annual equity and debt transactions. SJP intends to leverage Chung's capital markets and acquisition expertise to expand its Class A office, industrial, and residential portfolio across New York and New Jersey.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact. Personnel moves in regional acquisition leadership signal competitive talent shifts but do not directly affect supply, demand, capital availability, or costs. However, SJP's stated focus on residential expansion alongside office/industrial suggests the firm may accelerate multifamily acquisition activity in NY/NJ, a capital-rich but supply-constrained region.

stories.title: 205K-SF Luxury Car Garage Planned for N. Scottsdale
stories.excerpt: Toy Barn’s 205,000-square-foot, six-building luxury car garage location is on track to begin construction within the 124-acre Mack Innovation Park in north Scottsdale. The Phoenix Business Journal reports the garage will sit on 10 acres of land off Loop 101, between Bell and Pima roads. It’s the company’s eighth and largest Phoenix-area location. The first 5-acre phase will break ground in the spring of 2027 with an anticipated completion date in the following spring. That phase will include a $35 million capital investment, 98,000 square feet with 64 suites, and a 6,000-square-foot community clubhouse. The second phase could break ground in the fall of 2027. In total, there will be 135 garage condos. Toy Barn opened its first location in 2010. It now has multiple facilities in Scottsdale, Chandler and Cave Creek with a 138,000-square-foot Dove Valley facility set to open in October. The 91-suite complex is already 85% sold out. DLR Group is the architect. The post 205K-SF Luxury Car Garage Planned for N. Scottsdale appeared first on Connect CRE.

stories.summary: Toy Barn is developing a 205,000-square-foot, six-building luxury car garage facility on 10 acres within the 124-acre Mack Innovation Park in north Scottsdale, off Loop 101 between Bell and Pima roads. The first 5-acre phase will begin construction in spring 2027 with a $35 million investment, delivering 98,000 square feet of space with 64 garage suites and a 6,000-square-foot community clubhouse by spring 2028. A second phase may follow in fall 2027, with a total of 135 garage condos planned.
stories.impact: Minimal relevance to multifamily development. However, the scale of luxury automotive/experiential real estate investment in north Scottsdale's emerging mixed-use corridor (Mack Innovation Park) signals demographic and purchasing-power strength in the submarket, which can support adjacent rental housing demand from affluent renters and validate development density assumptions for multifamily projects in the Loop 101 corridor.

stories.title: Mesa West Capital Provides $81M Refi for Colorado Multifamily Complex
stories.excerpt: A joint venture between the Dinerstein Companies and PGIM has secured $81 million to refinance Atlas Peakview, a 330-unit multifamily complex that recently opened outside Denver, Colo., Commercial Observer can first report. Mesa West Capital provided the debt, structured as a short-term, first-mortgage loan, while Walker & Dunlop’s Tom Melody and Paul House arranged the transaction. Also involved was John Melody, who recently left Walker & Dunlop for Transwestern. Brian Hirsh, head of Mesa West Capital’s central region, noted in a statement that Atlas Peakview has experienced positive leasing metrics since opening in 2025, as it reached 85 percent occupancy by only the second quarter last year. “Our financing will provide the sponsor with a fresh runway as it continues to capitalize on robust demand from renters seeking high-quality, amenity-rich housing in a desirable Denver Tech Center location,” said Hirsh. Located at 7800 East Peakview Avenue in the Denver suburb of Centennial, Atlas Peakview features a mix of apartment units ranging from studios to three-bedrooms. The asset is near Interstate 25 and is only 13 miles southeast of downtown Denver. On-site amenities include a resort-style pool, an outdoor cooking area, a sky lounge, a fitness center, a media center, a pet-wash station, and a speakeasy-style bar. The financing for Atlas Peakview marks yet another short-term mortgage loan for Mesa West, which has originated $800 million in short-term debt in the first six months of 2026. “Mesa West continues to finance high-quality assets in well-located markets with durable demand drivers and improving operating fundamentals,” said Steve Fried, head of originations at Mesa West. Brian Pascus can be reached at bpascus@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Mesa West Capital provides $81M short-term refi for Atlas Peakview, 330-unit new multifamily in Centennial, CO (Denver metro)
JV Dinerstein Companies and PGIM; property achieved 85% occupancy by Q2 2025, demonstrating strong leasing momentum
Denver Tech Center location with high-quality amenities; financing validates post-stabilization refinance market
stories.summary: Mesa West Capital provided an $81 million short-term, first-mortgage refinance for Atlas Peakview, a 330-unit multifamily community developed by a joint venture of Dinerstein Companies and PGIM in Centennial, Colorado (Denver Tech Center area). The newly opened property achieved 85% occupancy by Q2 2025, demonstrating strong leasing dynamics. The transaction was arranged by Walker & Dunlop's Tom Melody and Paul House.
stories.impact: Signals robust capital availability and appetite for newly stabilized multifamily in the Denver Tech Center submarket; strong leasing velocity (85% occupancy at stabilization) validates continued rental demand strength in suburban Denver. Refinance execution at favorable terms reflects lender confidence in Tech Center fundamentals and de-risks future development capital sourcing for similar projects in the Denver metro, supporting pipeline expansion.

stories.title: Invesco Reports Stronger Earnings in Q2 With 20% Revenue Jump
stories.excerpt: Investment management firm Invesco reported better-than-expected earnings results for the second quarter of 2026. During the second quarter, Invesco posted adjusted income of $322.3 million, or 71 cents per share, comfortably above the Zacks Consensus estimate of 67 cents per share. Invesco also reported that its QQQ fund, the firm’s privately managed, exchange-traded fund (ETF), brought in $13.8 billion of net inflows. “In the first half of 2026, the Qs’ AUM grew 20 percent and it produced strong organic net flow growth in the second quarter,” Schlossberg said. “We have significant opportunities to continue to expand this flagship, competitively advantaged product, not only here in the United States, where the traction is incredibly strong, but also in other international markets.” The QQQ fund is now cross-listed on both the Hong Kong and Tokyo stock exchanges, and has raised $10 billion of AUM there so far. “We see several avenues to continue to expand QQQ’s client base, our innovation suite in general, and our wider $1.25 trillion ETF complex,” Schlossberg continued. bullets: Invesco reports Q2 2026 adjusted net revenue of $1.83B, +20% YoY; earnings beat consensus by $0.04/share
Assets under management (AUM) reached $2.5T, +14.4% YoY; CEO cites momentum in executing strategic priorities

stories.summary: Invesco reported better-than-expected Q2 2026 earnings, posting adjusted net revenue of $1.83 billion (up more than 20% from $1.52 billion in Q2 2025) and adjusted earnings of 71 cents per share, beating consensus of 67 cents. Assets under management reached $2.5 trillion at quarter-end, a 14.4% increase from Q2 2025. CEO Andrew Schlossberg attributed the performance to strong execution of strategic priorities and broad client demand for diversified products in uncertain markets.
stories.impact: Minimal direct relevance to multifamily development. However, Invesco's strong earnings and AUM growth (particularly via ETFs like QQQ) reflect robust institutional capital availability and risk appetite, which indirectly supports multifamily debt and equity capital markets. Increased AUM and investor confidence can lower hurdle rates and expand financing availability for quality multifamily sponsors.
